faq.a: Aazam is associated with the Arabic form أعظم, whose core sense is great, mighty, sublime, magnificent.

faq.q: What is the origin of Aazam?
faq.a: Aazam is associated with Arabic. Elative of عظيم (ʿaẓīm, 'great'). The source record's form عظم is the root rather than the name form.
Yes — the underlying form أعظم is Arabic.
Aazam can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Aazam should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. root ع ظ م occurs in the Qur'an; أعظم is the elative of عظيم ('greater, greatest'), a normal Arabic word

faq.q: What does Aazam mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Aazam is rendered اعظم and carries the sense عظیم، بلند، بزرگ.

faq.q: What does Aazam mean in Persian?
faq.a: No verified Persian form was established for Aazam.

faq.q: What are the variants of Aazam?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Aazam, aazam, azam. Script forms are أعظم, اعظم, आज़म.

faq.q: Is Aazam a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
